questions.question: Amazon SDE Interview: In the "Number of Islands" grid problem (where '1' is land and '0' is water), what is the time complexity to count islands using Breadth First Search (BFS)?
questions.explanation: BFS (or DFS) visits every cell in the M x N grid at most twice (once during outer scan and once during queue processing), yielding O(M * N) time and O(min(M, N)) auxiliary queue space.

questions.question: Amazon Coding Round: In "Rotting Oranges" (multi-source BFS), why must all initial rotten oranges be pushed into the queue at minute 0 simultaneously?
questions.explanation: Multi-source BFS simulates parallel spreading of contamination level-by-level across time, ensuring that the minimum elapsed minutes to rot all adjacent fresh oranges is found correctly.

questions.question: Amazon Coding Round: How can the running Median of a continuous stream of numbers be computed in O(1) query time and O(log N) insertion time?
questions.explanation: Maintain two heaps: a Max-Heap for the lower half of numbers and a Min-Heap for the upper half. Balances sizes so difference <= 1. Median is top of larger heap (or average of both tops if sizes are equal).

questions.question: Amazon Systems (DynamoDB): In Amazon DynamoDB table design, what is the role of the Partition Key (Hash Key) vs Sort Key (Range Key)?
questions.explanation: The Partition Key determines the physical storage partition via internal hashing, while the Sort Key orders items within that same partition, enabling fast range queries.

questions.question: Amazon SDE Round: In the "Course Schedule" problem (prerequisite courses [u, v]), what algorithm detects if it is possible to finish all courses?
questions.explanation: Course prerequisites form a directed graph. Finishing all courses is possible if and only if the graph contains NO directed cycles, detected via Topological Sorting (Kahn's algorithm or DFS 3-coloring).

questions.question: Amazon Coding Round: In the "Minimum Window Substring" problem (find minimum window in S containing all characters of T), which pattern achieves O(|S| + |T|) time complexity?
questions.explanation: A variable-size Sliding Window with a character frequency map and a matched counter expands right until all characters are satisfied, then shrinks left to find minimal valid length in O(|S| + |T|).

questions.question: Amazon Leadership & Architecture: To ensure that an API request (e.g. charging a payment or placing an order) is processed safely without duplicate charges if retried, what concept is implemented?
questions.explanation: Idempotency: Client supplies a unique Idempotency-Key. The backend records this key and returns the cached result for identical retries, preventing duplicate transactions.

questions.question: Amazon Coding Round: In the "Top K Frequent Elements" problem for an array of size N, what algorithm runs in O(N) linear time without sorting?
questions.explanation: Bucket Sort: Count element frequencies in a hash map (max frequency is N). Create buckets array of size N+1 where index is frequency. Traverse buckets from right to left to collect top K in O(N) time.

questions.question: Amazon Coding Round: In "Word Search" on an M x N board of characters, how is letter reuse prevented within the same word search path during DFS backtracking?
questions.explanation: Temporarily mark the board cell with a sentinel character (e.g. board[r][c] = '#') during recursion, and restore original character upon returning (backtracking). Runs in O(1) extra space.

questions.question: Amazon SDE Coding: What is the optimal time complexity to calculate the maximum sum of a path between any two nodes in a Binary Tree (Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum)?
questions.explanation: Postorder DFS: for each node, compute max contribution from left and right children (max(0, gain)). Update globalMax with (node.val + leftGain + rightGain). Returns node.val + max(leftGain, rightGain). Runs in strictly O(N) time.

questions.question: Amazon SDE Assessment [Set 1]: In the Reorganize String problem (rearrange so no two adjacent characters are identical), what data structure greedily places the most frequent characters first?
questions.explanation: A Max-Heap prioritized by character count pops the most frequent character, appends it, and temporarily holds it aside until the next distinct character is placed.

questions.question: Amazon SDE Assessment [Set 1]: In Container With Most Water (array of heights), why is the pointer pointing to the shorter height always moved inward?
questions.explanation: The width decreases by 1 on every move. Moving the taller pointer cannot increase the area (it is bottlenecked by the shorter line). Only moving the shorter pointer has potential to find a taller line to overcome width loss.
tags: Container With Most Water Two Pointers

questions.question: Amazon SDE Assessment [Set 1]: In the Meeting Rooms II problem (finding minimum conference rooms required for overlapping meeting intervals), how does a Min-Heap help?
questions.explanation: Sort intervals by start time. A Min-Heap stores end times of active meetings. If current meeting start >= heap.peek(), the room is reused (heap.pop()). Otherwise, a new room is allocated. Heap size is min rooms needed.

questions.question: Amazon SDE Assessment [Set 1]: In an N x N matrix where every row and column is sorted in ascending order, how is the K-th smallest element found in O(N log(max - min)) time?
questions.explanation: Binary Search on the answer range [min, max]: for each mid, count elements <= mid in O(N) using a staircase scan from bottom-left or top-right. Adjust binary search bounds accordingly.
tags: Kth Smallest Element in Sorted Matrix

questions.question: Amazon SDE Assessment [Set 1]: In Amazon e-commerce high-throughput caching, why is an LRU cache implemented with thread-safe Read-Write Locks rather than synchronized methods?
questions.explanation: Read-Write Locks (e.g. ReentrantReadWriteLock) allow multiple concurrent readers to access cache entries simultaneously without blocking each other, locking exclusively only for write/eviction operations.

questions.question: Amazon SDE Assessment [Set 1]: When cloning an Amazon product recommendation network (an undirected graph with cycles), what is stored in the visited hash map?
questions.explanation: The map stores originalNode -> clonedNode. This allows instant retrieval of cloned references when encountering already-visited nodes, breaking infinite cycles in O(V + E) time.

questions.question: Amazon SDE Assessment [Set 1]: In finding the number of contiguous subarrays where product of elements is strictly less than k (all elements > 0), what does (right - left + 1) represent?
questions.explanation: For each valid window [left, right], (right - left + 1) is the exact number of new subarrays ending at index right that satisfy the product condition.
tags: Sliding Window Subarray Product Less Than K

questions.question: Amazon SDE Assessment [Set 1]: In Lowest Common Ancestor of a General Binary Tree (not a BST), what is returned when p is found in the left subtree and q is found in the right subtree?
questions.explanation: If left recursion returns non-null (p found) and right recursion returns non-null (q found), current node is the lowest common divergence point and is returned as the LCA.

questions.question: Amazon SDE Assessment [Set 1]: In Course Schedule II, if the total number of elements popped from Kahn's topological sorting queue is less than total courses numCourses, what does this indicate?
questions.explanation: If queue empties before all nodes are processed, the graph contains a directed cycle (circular dependency), making a complete topological ordering impossible (return empty array).

questions.question: Amazon SDE Assessment [Set 1]: Amazon Logistics SDE: Given CPU tasks represented by characters and cooldown period n, what formula gives the minimum total intervals required?
questions.explanation: max((maxFreq - 1) * (n + 1) + countOfMaxFreqTasks, totalTasks). The most frequent tasks define the frame structure, and remaining tasks fill empty idle slots.

questions.question:
Capgemini Pseudocode Round:
What is the output of the following pseudocode?
Integer a = 5, b = 10, c
c = (a & b) + (a | b) + (a ^ b)
Print c

Capgemini Technical MCQ: What is the output of the following pseudocode?
Integer p = 8, q = 3
p = p >> 1
q = q << 2
Print p + q

Capgemini Pseudocode: What will be printed by the following code snippet?
Integer x = 1, y = 1
While(x <= 4)
  y = y * x
  x = x + 1
End While
Print y
questions.explanation: The loop computes the factorial of 4: y starts at 1, multiplied by 1, 2, 3, 4 sequentially. y = 1 * 1 * 2 * 3 * 4 = 24.

questions.question: Capgemini Technical Competency: In Cloud Computing, which service model provides virtualized computing resources (VMs, storage, and firewalls) over the internet?
questions.explanation: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) provides virtual machines, raw storage, and virtual networking (e.g. AWS EC2, Azure VMs, Google Compute Engine).

questions.question:
Capgemini Pseudocode: What will be the output of the following recursive function for fun(4)?
Integer fun(Integer n)
  If(n == 0 || n == 1)
    Return 1
  End If
  Return fun(n - 1) + fun(n - 2)
End Function
questions.explanation: This generates the Fibonacci sequence: fun(0)=1, fun(1)=1, fun(2)=2, fun(3)=3, fun(4)=fun(3)+fun(2)=3+2=5.

questions.question: Capgemini Technical Round: Which data structure is used by the system compiler to implement function call and return address management?
questions.explanation: The Call Stack (LIFO data structure) stores activation records (stack frames) containing return addresses, function parameters, and local variables.

questions.question:
Capgemini Pseudocode: What is the output of the following pseudocode?
Integer a = 12, b = 6, c = 2
a = a / b / c
Print a
questions.explanation: Division associates from left to right: (12 / 6) / 2 = 2 / 2 = 1.

questions.question: Capgemini DBMS MCQ: Which relational database operation is equivalent to a Cartesian product followed by a selection condition?
questions.explanation: Theta Join (or Inner Join) is formally defined in relational algebra as a Cartesian Product (Cross Join) followed by a selection (sigma) on the join predicate.

questions.question:
Capgemini Pseudocode: What is the value of count after execution?
Integer count = 0, i, j
For(i = 1 to 4)
  For(j = 1 to i)
    count = count + 1
  End For
End For
Print count
questions.explanation: When i=1: 1 iteration. i=2: 2 iterations. i=3: 3 iterations. i=4: 4 iterations. Total count = 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10.

questions.question: Capgemini Technical MCQ: What is the average-case time complexity of searching an element in a balanced Binary Search Tree containing N nodes?
questions.explanation: In a balanced BST (like AVL or Red-Black Tree), each comparison cuts the remaining search space by half, resulting in O(log N) average and worst-case time complexity.

Integer a = 7, b = 4, c = 2
c = (a & b) ^ (b | c)
Print c
Capgemini Technical Assessment [Module 1]: In an array of size N, what is the new index of an element initially at index i after rotating the array to the right by K positions?
questions.explanation: Right rotation by K positions places element at new index = (i + K) % N.

questions.question: Capgemini Technical Assessment [Module 1]: In Capgemini Technical Round: Which data structure evaluates prefix (Polish) and postfix (Reverse Polish) expressions in linear time?
questions.explanation: A Stack is used: for postfix, scan left-to-right pushing operands and popping two on operators. For prefix, scan right-to-left.

questions.question: Capgemini Technical Assessment [Module 1]: What optimization allows Bubble Sort to terminate in O(N) time when the input array is already sorted?
questions.explanation: Using a boolean swapped flag: if no swaps occur during the first pass (swapped == false), the array is already sorted and the algorithm terminates immediately in O(N) time.

questions.question: Capgemini Technical Assessment [Module 1]: In C programming: What happens to a static local variable inside a function between consecutive function calls?
questions.explanation: A static local variable retains its value across function calls because it is allocated in the static data segment and initialized only once when the program loads.

questions.question: Capgemini Technical Assessment [Module 1]: In relational databases (SQL), how does a PRIMARY KEY differ from a UNIQUE KEY constraint?
questions.explanation: A table can have only one PRIMARY KEY and it strictly forbids NULL values. A table can have multiple UNIQUE KEYs, which permit NULL values.
tags: DBMS Primary Key vs Unique Key

questions.question: Capgemini Technical Assessment [Module 1]: Which HTTP method in RESTful web services is used to update an existing resource idempotently (replacing the entire representation)?
questions.explanation: PUT is idempotent and replaces the entire resource. PATCH applies partial modifications. POST is non-idempotent and creates new resources.

questions.question: Capgemini Technical Assessment [Module 1]: In a circular queue of capacity N implemented via array with front and rear pointers, what condition indicates the queue is completely full?
questions.explanation: The queue is full when: (rear + 1) % N == front (leaving one vacant slot to distinguish full from empty where front == rear).

questions.question: Capgemini Technical Assessment [Module 1]: In C, how does a standard while loop calculate the length of a string without calling strlen()?
questions.explanation: Strings in C are null-terminated. Iterating while(str[len] != '\0') len++ counts characters until the null terminator is reached in O(N) time.

questions.question: Capgemini Technical Assessment [Module 1]: What are the best-case and worst-case time complexities of Linear Search on an array of size N?
questions.explanation: Best case is O(1) when the target element is at the very first index (index 0). Worst case is O(N) when the element is at the last index or absent.
tags: Linear Search Best vs Worst Case

questions.question: Capgemini Technical Assessment [Module 2]: What optimization allows Bubble Sort to terminate in O(N) time when the input array is already sorted?
questions.explanation: Using a boolean swapped flag: if no swaps occur during the first pass (swapped == false), the array is already sorted and the algorithm terminates immediately in O(N) time.

questions.question: Capgemini Technical Assessment [Module 2]: In C programming: What happens to a static local variable inside a function between consecutive function calls?
questions.explanation: A static local variable retains its value across function calls because it is allocated in the static data segment and initialized only once when the program loads.

questions.question: Capgemini Technical Assessment [Module 2]: In relational databases (SQL), how does a PRIMARY KEY differ from a UNIQUE KEY constraint?
questions.explanation: A table can have only one PRIMARY KEY and it strictly forbids NULL values. A table can have multiple UNIQUE KEYs, which permit NULL values.
tags: DBMS Primary Key vs Unique Key

questions.question: Capgemini Technical Assessment [Module 2]: Which HTTP method in RESTful web services is used to update an existing resource idempotently (replacing the entire representation)?
questions.explanation: PUT is idempotent and replaces the entire resource. PATCH applies partial modifications. POST is non-idempotent and creates new resources.

questions.question: Capgemini Technical Assessment [Module 2]: In a circular queue of capacity N implemented via array with front and rear pointers, what condition indicates the queue is completely full?
questions.explanation: The queue is full when: (rear + 1) % N == front (leaving one vacant slot to distinguish full from empty where front == rear).

questions.question: Capgemini Technical Assessment [Module 2]: In C, how does a standard while loop calculate the length of a string without calling strlen()?
questions.explanation: Strings in C are null-terminated. Iterating while(str[len] != '\0') len++ counts characters until the null terminator is reached in O(N) time.

questions.question: Capgemini Technical Assessment [Module 2]: What are the best-case and worst-case time complexities of Linear Search on an array of size N?
questions.explanation: Best case is O(1) when the target element is at the very first index (index 0). Worst case is O(N) when the element is at the last index or absent.
tags: Linear Search Best vs Worst Case

questions.question: Deloitte Analyst Interview: In SQL, which clause is specifically used to filter groups created by the GROUP BY statement based on an aggregate condition?
questions.explanation: HAVING is applied after grouping and aggregation, whereas WHERE filters individual rows before any grouping occurs.

questions.question: Deloitte Technical Round: What is the key difference between the SQL RANK() and DENSE_RANK() window functions when two rows share the same ranking value?
questions.explanation: RANK() leaves gaps in ranking numbers after duplicate values (e.g. 1, 2, 2, 4), whereas DENSE_RANK() does not skip rank values (e.g. 1, 2, 2, 3).

questions.question: Deloitte Advisory (Cyber Risk): In public-key cryptography (Asymmetric Encryption), which key is used by the sender to encrypt a confidential message intended only for the recipient?
questions.explanation: In asymmetric encryption, the sender encrypts using the recipient's public key. Only the recipient possesses the corresponding private key required to decrypt the message.

questions.question: Deloitte Systems MCQ: Which normal form eliminates partial functional dependencies (where a non-prime attribute depends on only a proper subset of a composite candidate key)?
questions.explanation: Second Normal Form (2NF) requires 1NF and guarantees that no non-prime attribute is functionally dependent on a proper subset of any candidate key (eliminates partial dependency).

questions.question: Deloitte Technical Interview: In the TCP 3-Way Handshake protocol, what packets are exchanged between client and server to establish a connection?
questions.explanation: 1) Client sends SYN. 2) Server responds with SYN-ACK. 3) Client acknowledges with ACK. The TCP connection is now established.

questions.question: Deloitte Database MCQ: What happens when you execute a TRUNCATE command compared to a DELETE command in a relational database?
questions.explanation: TRUNCATE is a DDL operation that deallocates all data pages, does not fire row-level triggers, cannot be filtered with WHERE, and is significantly faster than DELETE (which logs row-by-row deletions).

questions.question: Deloitte Web Services: What does an HTTP 504 status code returned by an API gateway indicate?
questions.explanation: HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout indicates that the server, while acting as a gateway or proxy, did not receive a timely response from the upstream server.

questions.question: Deloitte Analytics Round: What SQL operator is used to combine the results of two SELECT statements into a single result set while automatically removing duplicate rows?
questions.explanation: UNION combines queries and eliminates duplicates. UNION ALL combines queries without removing duplicates, making it faster when uniqueness is guaranteed or duplicates are desired.

questions.question: Deloitte Risk & Governance: In database transactions, what does the 'I' in ACID stand for, and what concurrency anomaly does it prevent?
questions.explanation: Isolation guarantees that concurrent transactions execute as if they were running serially without interfering with each other, preventing dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, and phantom reads.

questions.question: Deloitte Data Engineering: When designing a Star Schema in a Data Warehouse, what two types of tables are used?
questions.explanation: A Star Schema contains a central Fact Table (holding numerical quantitative measurements and foreign keys) surrounded by denormalized Dimension Tables (holding context attributes).

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 1]: In SQL, what distinguishes a Correlated Subquery from an uncorrelated regular subquery?
questions.explanation: A correlated subquery references columns from the outer query table, executing once for every candidate row evaluated by the outer query.

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 1]: Which OSI layer is responsible for end-to-end process-to-process communication, port addressing, flow control, and segmentation?
questions.explanation: The Transport Layer (Layer 4) handles end-to-end communication, port addressing (e.g. TCP/UDP ports), flow control, and error recovery. Network Layer (Layer 3) handles host-to-host IP routing.

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 1]: Why do relational database engines (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle) utilize B+ Trees rather than Binary Search Trees for on-disk table indexing?
questions.explanation: B+ trees have a high branching factor (fan-out), keeping tree height low (3-4 levels) to minimize expensive disk I/O, and all data pointers are stored in contiguous leaf nodes for efficient range scans.

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 1]: What does the SQL function COALESCE(val1, val2, val3, ...) return?
questions.explanation: COALESCE evaluates its arguments in order and returns the first non-NULL expression among them. If all expressions evaluate to NULL, it returns NULL.

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 1]: In DNS lookup for a domain name like www.example.com, what server is contacted first if the address is not found in the local OS cache or recursive resolver?
questions.explanation: The recursive resolver contacts the Root DNS Servers ('.'), which direct the query to the Top-Level Domain (TLD) servers ('.com'), which direct to the Authoritative Name Servers.

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 1]: Which SQL Transaction Isolation Level is the strictest, completely preventing Dirty Reads, Non-Repeatable Reads, and Phantom Reads?
questions.explanation: SERIALIZABLE is the highest isolation level. It executes transactions in a manner completely equivalent to serial serializable execution, preventing all concurrency anomalies.

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 1]: In database modeling, when is a SELF JOIN typically applied on a table?
questions.explanation: A Self Join joins a table to itself, commonly used to query hierarchical data stored in a single table, such as an Employee table with EmployeeID and ManagerID.

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 1]: In web application security, how is Stored or Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) effectively prevented?
questions.explanation: XSS is prevented by context-aware Output Encoding (escaping special characters like <, >, &), input validation, using secure web frameworks, and enforcing a strict Content Security Policy (CSP).

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 1]: Why is the EXISTS clause generally preferred over IN when subquery results are large or involve NULL values?
questions.explanation: EXISTS short-circuits: it stops scanning the subquery as soon as a single matching row is found (returns boolean true), avoiding full result set materialization, and handles NULLs predictably.

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 1]: What additional condition must be satisfied for a relation to be in Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) that is not strictly required by 3NF?
questions.explanation: In BCNF, for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y, X must be a Superkey. 3NF relaxes this condition if Y is a prime attribute (part of a candidate key).

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 2]: In SQL, what distinguishes a Correlated Subquery from an uncorrelated regular subquery?
questions.explanation: A correlated subquery references columns from the outer query table, executing once for every candidate row evaluated by the outer query.

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 2]: Which OSI layer is responsible for end-to-end process-to-process communication, port addressing, flow control, and segmentation?
questions.explanation: The Transport Layer (Layer 4) handles end-to-end communication, port addressing (e.g. TCP/UDP ports), flow control, and error recovery. Network Layer (Layer 3) handles host-to-host IP routing.

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 2]: Why do relational database engines (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle) utilize B+ Trees rather than Binary Search Trees for on-disk table indexing?
questions.explanation: B+ trees have a high branching factor (fan-out), keeping tree height low (3-4 levels) to minimize expensive disk I/O, and all data pointers are stored in contiguous leaf nodes for efficient range scans.

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 2]: What does the SQL function COALESCE(val1, val2, val3, ...) return?
questions.explanation: COALESCE evaluates its arguments in order and returns the first non-NULL expression among them. If all expressions evaluate to NULL, it returns NULL.

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 2]: In DNS lookup for a domain name like www.example.com, what server is contacted first if the address is not found in the local OS cache or recursive resolver?
questions.explanation: The recursive resolver contacts the Root DNS Servers ('.'), which direct the query to the Top-Level Domain (TLD) servers ('.com'), which direct to the Authoritative Name Servers.

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 2]: Which SQL Transaction Isolation Level is the strictest, completely preventing Dirty Reads, Non-Repeatable Reads, and Phantom Reads?
questions.explanation: SERIALIZABLE is the highest isolation level. It executes transactions in a manner completely equivalent to serial serializable execution, preventing all concurrency anomalies.

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 2]: In database modeling, when is a SELF JOIN typically applied on a table?
questions.explanation: A Self Join joins a table to itself, commonly used to query hierarchical data stored in a single table, such as an Employee table with EmployeeID and ManagerID.

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 2]: In web application security, how is Stored or Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) effectively prevented?
questions.explanation: XSS is prevented by context-aware Output Encoding (escaping special characters like <, >, &), input validation, using secure web frameworks, and enforcing a strict Content Security Policy (CSP).

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 2]: Why is the EXISTS clause generally preferred over IN when subquery results are large or involve NULL values?
questions.explanation: EXISTS short-circuits: it stops scanning the subquery as soon as a single matching row is found (returns boolean true), avoiding full result set materialization, and handles NULLs predictably.

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 2]: What additional condition must be satisfied for a relation to be in Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) that is not strictly required by 3NF?
questions.explanation: In BCNF, for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y, X must be a Superkey. 3NF relaxes this condition if Y is a prime attribute (part of a candidate key).

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 3]: In SQL, what distinguishes a Correlated Subquery from an uncorrelated regular subquery?
questions.explanation: A correlated subquery references columns from the outer query table, executing once for every candidate row evaluated by the outer query.

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 3]: Which OSI layer is responsible for end-to-end process-to-process communication, port addressing, flow control, and segmentation?
questions.explanation: The Transport Layer (Layer 4) handles end-to-end communication, port addressing (e.g. TCP/UDP ports), flow control, and error recovery. Network Layer (Layer 3) handles host-to-host IP routing.

questions.question: Deloitte Consulting Assessment [Practice 3]: Why do relational database engines (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle) utilize B+ Trees rather than Binary Search Trees for on-disk table indexing?
questions.explanation: B+ trees have a high branching factor (fan-out), keeping tree height low (3-4 levels) to minimize expensive disk I/O, and all data pointers are stored in contiguous leaf nodes for efficient range scans.

questions.question: Wipro Elite NLTH Coding: In Java string manipulation, what is the time complexity of reversing a string using StringBuilder.reverse() for a string of length N?
questions.explanation: StringBuilder.reverse() modifies the internal character array in-place using two pointers swapping from both ends, executing in O(N) time and O(1) extra space.

questions.question: Wipro Automata Fix: What is the issue with this C code for checking even numbers: "if (n & 1 == 0)"?
questions.explanation: In C operator precedence, "==" has higher precedence than bitwise "&". The expression evaluates as "n & (1 == 0)", which is always 0. Parentheses are required: "if ((n & 1) == 0)".

questions.question: Wipro Technical Round: In a singly linked list, which pointer operation inserts a new node temp after a given node curr?
questions.explanation: temp->next must point to curr->next first, then curr->next is updated to temp. If reversed, the rest of the list is permanently lost.

questions.question: Wipro NLTH MCQ: In an array of N integers, how many passes does Selection Sort take to completely sort the array in the worst case?
questions.explanation: Selection Sort always runs N - 1 passes, finding the minimum element in the remaining unsorted subarray and swapping it into place.

questions.question: Wipro Elite Technical: In Java OOP, what exception is thrown when attempting to access a method on an uninitialized reference variable pointing to null?
questions.explanation: Dereferencing null throws NullPointerException (NPE) at runtime in Java.

questions.question: Wipro Automata Coding: What is the optimal algorithm to check if two strings are anagrams of each other?
questions.explanation: Using a fixed-size frequency array of 256 characters: increment for string 1 and decrement for string 2. If all counts are 0, they are anagrams. Runs in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

questions.question: Wipro Technical MCQ: In C++, can a class constructor be declared as "virtual"?
questions.explanation: Constructors CANNOT be virtual in C++ because a virtual call requires an existing object with a valid vptr, but the vptr is only set up by the constructor during object creation.

questions.question: Wipro NLTH MCQ: Which data structure is used to implement a Breadth-First Traversal of a graph?
questions.explanation: BFS processes vertices in FIFO order, requiring a Queue data structure.

questions.question: Wipro Coding Round: What is the time complexity of finding the maximum element in an unsorted array of size N?
questions.explanation: Finding the maximum requires inspecting every element at least once, taking O(N) time.

questions.question: Wipro Technical Round: In database management, what constraint ensures that the value in a foreign key column must exist in the referenced primary key column?
questions.explanation: Referential Integrity Constraint enforces that foreign key values must match existing primary key values in the parent table or be NULL.

questions.question: Wipro Elite Technical: In multithreading, what is a Race Condition?
questions.explanation: A race condition occurs when multiple threads access and modify shared data concurrently, and the final outcome depends on the non-deterministic order of thread scheduling.

questions.question: Wipro Coding: What is the value of 1 << 5 in integer arithmetic?
questions.explanation: Left shifting 1 by 5 positions evaluates to 2^5 = 32.

questions.question: Wipro Automata Fix: In C, what does the expression *(arr + i) evaluate to for an integer array arr?
questions.explanation: In C pointer-subscript equivalence: *(arr + i) is completely identical to arr[i].

questions.question: Wipro Technical Round: In Object-Oriented Programming, what is Encapsulation?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation bundles data (fields) and the methods that operate on that data into a single unit (class), while restricting direct access to internal state via private access specifiers.

questions.question: Wipro NLTH MCQ: In an undirected graph with N vertices and N - 1 edges that is connected, what structure is formed?
questions.explanation: Any connected undirected graph with N vertices and N - 1 edges is strictly a Tree (acyclic connected graph).

questions.question:
Accenture Cognitive & Coding: In pseudocode, what is the output of:
Integer a = 3, b = 7
If ((a + b) > 8 && (b - a) < 5)
  Print a * b
Else
  Print a + b
End If
questions.explanation: (3 + 7) = 10 > 8 is True. (7 - 3) = 4 < 5 is True. Both conditions hold, so print a * b = 3 * 7 = 21.

questions.question: Accenture Technical MCQ: In Cloud Computing, which characteristic of cloud enables automatic scaling of resources up or down based on current traffic demands?
questions.explanation: Rapid Elasticity allows cloud services to dynamically provision and release resources automatically in response to demand fluctuations.

questions.question:
Accenture Pseudocode: What will be the value of sum after the loop executes?
Integer sum = 0, i
For(i = 1 to 5)
  If(i mod 2 == 0)
    sum = sum + i
  End If
End For
Print sum
questions.explanation: Even numbers in range [1, 5] are 2 and 4. sum = 2 + 4 = 6.

questions.question: Accenture Network Security: What type of firewall inspects data packets at the application layer to block SQL Injection and Cross-Site Scripting attacks?
questions.explanation: A Web Application Firewall (WAF) inspects Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS traffic to detect and block web vulnerabilities like SQLi and XSS.

questions.question: Accenture Coding Assessment: What is the time complexity to search an element in a Hash Table with open addressing in the best/average case vs worst case?
questions.explanation: Average case is O(1) with good hash distribution. Worst case is O(N) when all keys collide into the same probe sequence.

questions.question: Accenture Technical MCQ: What is the main purpose of the "try-catch-finally" block in Java?
questions.explanation: try encloses code that may throw exceptions; catch handles specific exceptions; finally executes guaranteed cleanup code (like closing streams) regardless of whether an exception occurred.

questions.question: Accenture Critical Reasoning: What is the next number in the series: 3, 8, 15, 24, 35, ...?

Accenture Pseudocode: What is printed?
Integer a = 2, b = 3
a = a ^ b
b = a ^ b
a = a ^ b
Print a, b
questions.explanation: This is the standard XOR swap algorithm. Swapping two integers without a temporary variable results in a = 3, b = 2.

questions.question: Accenture Technical MCQ: In Relational Databases, what SQL constraint ensures that all values in a column are distinct from one another?
questions.explanation: The UNIQUE constraint ensures that all values in a column are different across all rows.

questions.question: Accenture Coding Assessment: What is the space complexity of Depth First Search (DFS) on a binary tree with maximum depth H?
questions.explanation: DFS uses recursion or an explicit stack whose maximum memory allocation is proportional to the tree height H: O(H) auxiliary space.

questions.question: Accenture Cloud MCQ: In the DevOps lifecycle, what does CI/CD stand for?
questions.explanation: CI/CD stands for Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (or Continuous Deployment), automating code build, testing, and deployment pipelines.

questions.question: Accenture Technical MCQ: In C, what is the output of printf("%d", sizeof(char))?
questions.explanation: By C language specification, sizeof(char) is defined to be exactly 1 byte on all compliant platforms.

questions.question:
Accenture Pseudocode: What is the output of:
Integer x = 10, y = 20
If (x > y || y > 15)
  x = x + 5
End If
Print x
questions.explanation: x > y (10 > 20) is False. y > 15 (20 > 15) is True. In || (logical OR), False || True evaluates to True. Therefore, x = 10 + 5 = 15.

questions.question: Accenture Technical Round: What is Polymorphism in Object-Oriented Programming?
questions.explanation: Polymorphism (meaning "many forms") allows entities (methods, operators, objects) to perform different behaviors based on context or runtime object type.

questions.question: Accenture Coding: Which algorithm is fastest for checking whether an integer n is a power of 2?
questions.explanation: If n is a power of 2 (n > 0), its binary representation has exactly one set bit (e.g. 8 is 1000). Thus, (n > 0) && ((n & (n - 1)) == 0) checks it in O(1) time.

questions.question: Cognizant GenC Next: In Java collections, which List implementation provides O(1) time complexity for random element access via index?
questions.explanation: ArrayList is backed by a contiguous dynamic array, allowing O(1) direct random access via get(index). LinkedList requires O(N) traversal.

questions.question: Cognizant Coding Round: What is the time complexity of searching for an element in a sorted array of size N using Binary Search?
questions.explanation: Binary Search halves the search space on each iteration, achieving O(log N) worst-case time complexity.

questions.question: Cognizant Technical MCQ: In SQL, which aggregate function returns the total count of non-null rows in a column?
questions.explanation: COUNT(column_name) counts all rows with non-NULL values in that column. COUNT(*) counts all rows regardless of NULLs.

questions.question: Cognizant Technical Round: In C programming, what is the value of an uninitialized local variable with automatic storage duration?
questions.explanation: Local variables with automatic storage duration contain indeterminate (garbage) values until explicitly initialized.

questions.question: Cognizant GenC Coding: What is the optimal time complexity to remove duplicates from a sorted array in-place?
questions.explanation: Two Pointers technique scans in-place in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space, copying unique elements to the front.

questions.question: Cognizant Technical MCQ: What is the primary difference between method overloading and method overriding in Java?
questions.explanation: Overloading happens at compile time with different parameter lists in the same class. Overriding happens at runtime when a subclass redefines a superclass method with the exact same signature.

questions.question: Cognizant GenC Next: In a Max Heap of N elements, what is the time complexity to extract the maximum element?
questions.explanation: Extracting the root takes O(1), and restoring the heap property (heapify-down) takes O(log N) time.

questions.question: Cognizant Technical MCQ: Which networking protocol automatically assigns dynamic IP addresses to devices connecting to a local area network?
questions.explanation: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) automatically assigns IP addresses, subnet masks, and default gateways to client devices.

questions.question: Cognizant Coding: What does the following expression return in Java: ("Hello" == new String("Hello"))?
questions.explanation: The "==" operator compares object references (memory addresses). "Hello" is in the String Constant Pool, while new String(...) is in general heap memory. They have different addresses, so it returns false. (equals() returns true).

questions.question: Cognizant GenC Next: What is the height of a balanced binary tree with N nodes?
questions.explanation: A balanced binary tree has height O(log2 N).

questions.question: Cognizant Technical MCQ: What type of join returns all rows from the right table, along with matching rows from the left table (and NULL for non-matching left rows)?
questions.explanation: A RIGHT OUTER JOIN returns all records from the right table and matching records from the left table, padding NULLs where no match exists.

questions.question: Cognizant Coding: In recursion, what condition must be defined to prevent an infinite recursive loop resulting in a StackOverflowError?
questions.explanation: The Base Case specifies when the recursive calls should terminate, preventing infinite call stack growth.

questions.question: Cognizant Technical Round: What is the binary equivalent of decimal number 25?
Cognizant GenC Next: Which sorting algorithm is considered stable and guarantees O(N log N) worst-case time complexity?
questions.explanation: Merge Sort guarantees O(N log N) worst-case time and is stable (preserves the relative order of records with equal keys). Quick Sort is not stable and has O(N^2) worst-case.

questions.question: Cognizant Technical MCQ: In modern operating systems, what is Virtual Memory?
questions.explanation: Virtual memory is a memory management technique that creates an illusion of a large uniform address space using a combination of RAM and disk storage (paging/swap).

questionOptions.explanation: A Queue operates under FIFO (First In First Out) semantics, which would evaluate operators in the exact order they appear, violating mathematical precedence rules.
A Stack maintains operators and pops them according to precedence (LIFO), which is the foundation of Dijkstra's Shunting-Yard algorithm.
A Binary Search Tree orders elements by value, not by operator precedence or expression sequence, resulting in O(N log N) overhead.
A Linked List provides bidirectional traversal but does not enforce automatic LIFO precedence resolution.

questionOptions.option_text: O(N) comparisons because all elements might need examination in the worst case.
questionOptions.explanation: O(N) is the complexity of Linear Search on an unsorted list. Binary Search guarantees discarding half the remaining elements each step.

questionOptions.option_text: O(N log N) comparisons due to recursive tree partitioning.
questionOptions.explanation: O(N log N) is typical for comparison-based sorting algorithms like Merge Sort, not binary search lookup.

questionOptions.option_text: O(log2 N) comparisons because the search space is divided by 2 at each step.
questionOptions.explanation: With each comparison, the search range [low, high] is cut in half. The maximum depth of the search decision tree is floor(log2 N) + 1.

questionOptions.option_text: O(1) constant comparisons because the middle index is checked immediately.
questionOptions.explanation: O(1) is the best-case time when the target happens to be at the exact middle index on the first check, not the worst-case.

questionOptions.option_text: Min-Heap of size 100 with O(log 100) insertion per element.
questionOptions.explanation: By storing the 100 largest elements in a Min-Heap, the root is always the 100th largest. If a new number is greater than the root, replace the root and heapify down in O(log 100) steps.

questionOptions.option_text: Max-Heap of size 10,000,000 with O(log N) insertion per element.
questionOptions.explanation: A Max-Heap of size N consumes massive memory (all 10 million elements) and takes O(log N) per insert instead of bounded O(log K).

questionOptions.option_text: Sorted Array of size 100 with O(100) linear shift per element.
questionOptions.explanation: While memory is small, inserting into a sorted array requires shifting up to 100 elements in O(K) time, which is slower than O(log K).

questionOptions.option_text: Hash Map storing counts of all numbers with O(1) lookup.
questionOptions.explanation: A Hash Map does not maintain ordering. Finding the top 100 from an unordered map would require sorting or an O(N) selection algorithm on every query.

questionOptions.option_text: Always transfer all elements from S1 to S2 on every Enqueue and transfer back.
questionOptions.explanation: Transferring back and forth on every single push makes Enqueue strictly O(N) worst-case and amortized, which is inefficient.

questionOptions.option_text: Push to S1 on Enqueue; Pop from S2 on Dequeue (transferring S1 to S2 only when S2 is empty).
questionOptions.explanation: S1 acts as the inbox and S2 acts as the outbox. Because each element enters S1 once and leaves S2 once, the amortized cost per operation across any sequence of N operations is strictly O(1).

questionOptions.option_text: Keep S1 sorted at all times by popping into S2 on every read.
questionOptions.explanation: Sorting stacks requires O(N^2) or O(N log N) operations and defeats the purpose of queue emulation.

questionOptions.option_text: It is mathematically impossible to achieve amortized O(1) Dequeue using only two stacks.
questionOptions.explanation: Amortized O(1) queue using two stacks is a canonical algorithmic technique proven via aggregate analysis.

questionOptions.option_text: QuickSort always runs in strictly O(N) linear time for arrays under 100,000 items.
questionOptions.explanation: Comparison-based sorting has a mathematical lower bound of Omega(N log N). QuickSort cannot run in O(N) general time.

questionOptions.option_text: MergeSort is unstable, while QuickSort is guaranteed to be stable.
questionOptions.explanation: The reverse is true: standard MergeSort is stable, whereas in-place QuickSort is naturally unstable due to long-distance swaps across the pivot.

questionOptions.option_text: QuickSort sorts in-place with O(1) auxiliary memory and exhibits exceptional CPU cache locality.
questionOptions.explanation: QuickSort accesses contiguous memory addresses sequentially, maximizing L1/L2 cache hits. MergeSort requires allocating and copying into an auxiliary array of size O(N).

questionOptions.option_text: QuickSort never makes recursive function calls.
questionOptions.explanation: QuickSort is fundamentally recursive (partitioning left and right sub-arrays) requiring O(log N) stack frames.

questionOptions.option_text: O(N) time with O(1) extra space using Sliding Window.
questionOptions.explanation: As the window slides right, updating the sum takes current_sum += arr[i] - arr[i-K]. Exactly N - K updates are performed in O(1) each.

questionOptions.option_text: O(N * K) time by recomputing the sum of every K-length slice from scratch.
questionOptions.explanation: Recomputing each window from scratch is the naive brute-force method, which is redundant because adjacent windows share K-1 elements.

questionOptions.option_text: O(N log N) time by sorting all subarrays.
questionOptions.explanation: Subarrays must maintain contiguous order; sorting would destroy their original positional indices.

questionOptions.option_text: O(K^2) time using dynamic programming tabulation.
questionOptions.explanation: DP is unnecessary here; simple pointer shifting achieves optimal linear time.

questionOptions.option_text: Sort the array and scan adjacent pairs in O(N log N) time.
questionOptions.explanation: Sorting requires O(N log N) time, which violates the O(N) linear time requirement.

questionOptions.option_text: Use a Hash Set to track seen numbers, removing on repeat in O(N) space.
questionOptions.explanation: Using a Hash Set achieves O(N) time but requires O(N) auxiliary space, violating the O(1) space constraint.

questionOptions.option_text: Compute the product of all elements and divide by duplicate factors.
questionOptions.explanation: Product calculations will overflow 64-bit integers almost immediately for arrays of size > 20.

questionOptions.option_text: XOR all elements together; duplicate pairs cancel to 0, leaving the unique number.
questionOptions.explanation: Because A ^ A = 0 and A ^ 0 = A, XORing all array elements results in (x1 ^ x1) ^ (x2 ^ x2) ^ ... ^ unique = 0 ^ unique = unique in O(N) time and O(1) space.

questionOptions.option_text: Sort activities by earliest Start Time.
questionOptions.explanation: Choosing the earliest start time fails if that activity is very long (e.g., from 8 AM to 8 PM), blocking many shorter activities.

questionOptions.option_text: Sort activities by earliest Finish Time.
questionOptions.explanation: Finishing an activity as early as possible frees up the resource immediately, greedily leaving the largest possible continuous window for remaining tasks.
Choosing the shortest duration can fail when a short activity overlaps with the middle of two other compatible activities.

questionOptions.option_text: Sort activities by fewest overlapping conflicts.
questionOptions.explanation: Minimizing conflicts is a heuristic that does not guarantee an optimal solution for all interval arrangements.

questionOptions.option_text: Stack depth is O(2^N), and time complexity is O(N^2).
questionOptions.explanation: Stack depth represents the maximum active function frames down any path, which is bounded by N, not 2^N.

questionOptions.option_text: Stack depth is O(1), and time complexity is O(N).
questionOptions.explanation: Tower of Hanoi cannot run in linear time because every single disk move must be printed, which takes 2^N - 1 operations.

questionOptions.option_text: Stack depth is O(N), and time complexity is O(2^N).
questionOptions.explanation: The recurrence is T(N) = 2T(N-1) + 1, which expands to 2^N - 1 operations. At any point, at most N frames are on the call stack.

questionOptions.option_text: Stack depth is O(log N), and time complexity is O(N log N).
questionOptions.explanation: O(log N) depth applies to divide-and-conquer where the problem size halves (N/2), whereas Hanoi reduces size by 1 (N-1).

questionOptions.option_text: When keys are inserted in sorted order (skewed tree); avoided using self-balancing trees like AVL or Red-Black trees.
questionOptions.explanation: Inserting already sorted data [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] makes every node a right child, turning height into N. Self-balancing trees perform tree rotations to keep height bounded by O(log N).

questionOptions.option_text: When all keys are identical; avoided using hash tables.
questionOptions.explanation: Standard BSTs either disallow duplicates or store count frequencies, which does not degrade search traversal.

questionOptions.option_text: When the tree has an odd number of nodes; avoided using complete binary trees.
questionOptions.explanation: Odd or even node parity has no influence on tree height or traversal efficiency.

questionOptions.option_text: A BST search never degrades to O(N) because binary search always guarantees O(log N).
questionOptions.explanation: Binary Search guarantees O(log N) on contiguous arrays. A BST only guarantees O(height), which can become O(N) if unbalanced.
Linear probing probes sequential slots (i, i+1, i+2...), which causes severe primary clustering as adjacent occupied blocks merge into long chains.
Quadratic probing uses quadratic steps (c1*i + c2*i^2), eliminating primary clustering, but keys that hash to the same starting slot still follow identical probe sequences (secondary clustering).

Double hashing uses two independent hash functions where the step size is h2(key). This ensures distinct probe paths even for keys with the same initial hash, eliminating primary and secondary clustering.
Separate chaining is a closed-addressing (open hashing) scheme where entries are stored in external linked lists, not open addressing.
O(N * L) would be the brute-force search time comparing against all N words in a list; a Trie avoids this by sharing common prefixes.
In a Trie, each character of the word corresponds to one edge traversal in O(1) time. Searching a word of length L requires exactly L operations, strictly independent of total stored words N.
O(log N) would apply to binary search in a sorted array of words, but a Trie does not perform binary search on nodes.
Sigma represents the alphabet size. With direct array indexing (children[char - "a"]), the transition takes O(1) time, not O(Sigma).
O(log N) is the time complexity when using only Union by Rank without Path Compression.
O(N) occurs only in naive Disjoint Sets without optimizations where tree structures degenerate into linear chains.

questionOptions.option_text: O(alpha(N)) where alpha is the Inverse Ackermann function
questionOptions.explanation: The combination of path compression (which flattens trees during find) and union by rank (which bounds tree height) achieves O(alpha(N)) amortized time, which is practically <= 4 for all physical inputs.

questionOptions.option_text: O(1) strict worst-case for every single operation
questionOptions.explanation: Individual operations can take longer than O(1) due to path compression traversal; the bound is amortized across operations, not strict worst-case.

codingProblems.title: Two Sum
codingProblems.description:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, find the two numbers in the array such that they add up to `target`.

Return their indices formatted as space-separated 0-indexed integers in ascending order.

You may assume that each input will have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.
codingProblems.constraints:
2 <= nums.length <= 10^4
-10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
-10^9 <= target <= 10^9
Only one valid answer exists.

starterCode.python:
import sys

def solve():
    lines = sys.stdin.read().strip().split('\n')
    if len(lines) < 2:
        return
    nums = list(map(int, lines[0].split()))
    target = int(lines[1].strip())

    # TODO: Find the two indices in nums whose values sum to target.
    # Print the 0-indexed indices separated by space, e.g., "0 1".
    pass

if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

knowledgeDocuments.title: Mastering Database Normalization (1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF) for Placement Interviews
knowledgeDocuments.summary: Comprehensive viva guide on eliminating anomalies (insertion, deletion, update) in relational schemas with clear interview examples.
knowledgeDocuments.content:
Database Normalization is the systematic technique of organizing data in a relational database to minimize redundancy and eliminate anomalous dependencies (Insertion, Update, and Deletion anomalies).

Key Normal Forms for Technical Interviews:
1. First Normal Form (1NF):
   - Every column must hold atomic (indivisible) values.
   - No repeating groups or arrays stored in a single attribute.
   - A primary key must uniquely identify each record.

2. Second Normal Form (2NF):
   - Relation must be in 1NF.
   - Eliminates Partial Dependency: Every non-prime attribute must be fully functionally dependent on the entire primary key, not a proper subset of it.
   - Note: If the primary key consists of only a single attribute, the relation is automatically in 2NF if in 1NF!

3. Third Normal Form (3NF):
   - Relation must be in 2NF.
   - Eliminates Transitive Dependency: For every functional dependency X -> A, either X is a Super Key or A is a prime attribute. Non-prime attributes cannot determine other non-prime attributes.
   - Standard placement interview question: "Why is 3NF preferred over BCNF in industry?" Answer: 3NF guarantees dependency preservation while achieving lossless join decomposition.

4. Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF / 3.5NF):
   - Stricter version of 3NF. For every functional dependency X -> A, X MUST be a Super Key without exception.

Common Interview Trap:
Candidate key vs Super key: A superkey is any set of attributes that uniquely identifies a row; a candidate key is a minimal superkey containing no redundant attributes.

knowledgeDocuments.title: ACID Properties, Isolation Levels and Deadlock Handling in Production DBMS
knowledgeDocuments.summary: Interview-ready breakdown of transaction management, isolation anomalies and Two-Phase Locking (2PL).
knowledgeDocuments.content:
A database transaction is a logical unit of work that must satisfy ACID properties:
- Atomicity: "All or nothing" execution. Managed via Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) and Undo logs.
- Consistency: The database must transition from one valid state to another, preserving all integrity constraints and foreign keys.
- Isolation: Concurrent transactions must execute without mutual interference.
- Durability: Once a transaction commits, its modifications are permanently recorded even in the event of power outage or system crash (via Redo logs and checkpointing).

SQL Isolation Levels & Prevented Read Phenomena:
1. Read Uncommitted: Suffers from Dirty Reads, Non-Repeatable Reads, Phantom Reads.
2. Read Committed (Postgres default): Prevents Dirty Reads.
3. Repeatable Read (MySQL default): Prevents Dirty Reads and Non-Repeatable Reads.
4. Serializable: Prevents all anomalies including Phantom Reads via strict 2-Phase Locking (2PL) or SSI.

knowledgeDocuments.title: Operating Systems: Virtual Memory, Paging, Page Fault Handling & Thrashing
knowledgeDocuments.summary: Virtual memory concepts explained with memory management unit (MMU), Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB), and Belady's anomaly.
knowledgeDocuments.content:
Virtual Memory maps large virtual address spaces onto smaller physical RAM frames using Paging.
- Logical Address is divided into: Page Number (p) and Offset (d).
- TLB (Translation Lookaside Buffer): High-speed hardware associative cache that stores recently accessed page-to-frame translations to avoid memory access penalties.
- Page Fault: Occurs when a referenced page is not currently resident in physical RAM (valid bit = 0 in Page Table). The CPU triggers a trap to OS kernel.
- Thrashing: Occurs when an OS spends more CPU cycles paging data in and out of swap space than executing productive process instructions. Occurs when sum of working sets exceeds total physical RAM.
- Belady's Anomaly: In FIFO page replacement, increasing the number of physical page frames can paradoxically increase the number of page faults. Optimal and LRU page replacement policies never exhibit Belady's Anomaly.

knowledgeDocuments.summary: Core technical questions for electronics engineers appearing for embedded hardware and IT technical rounds.
knowledgeDocuments.content:
Core ECE Technical Viva Questions:
1. 8085 Microprocessor Highlights:
   - 8-bit data bus, 16-bit address bus (can address up to 64 KB of memory).
   - Clock frequency: typically 3 MHz (internal clock generated by dividing crystal frequency by 2).
   - Flags: Sign (S), Zero (Z), Auxiliary Carry (AC), Parity (P), Carry (CY).

2. 8085 Interrupt Hierarchy (Highest to Lowest Priority):
   - TRAP (Non-Maskable, Vectored at 0024H)
   - RST 7.5 (Maskable, Edge-triggered, Vectored at 003CH)
   - RST 6.5 (Maskable, Level-triggered, Vectored at 0034H)
   - RST 5.5 (Maskable, Level-triggered, Vectored at 002CH)
   - INTR (Maskable, Non-vectored)

3. Difference between Microprocessor and Microcontroller:
   - Microprocessor contains ALU, Registers and Control Unit; external RAM, ROM and I/O ports must be connected.
   - Microcontroller has CPU, RAM, ROM, Timers and I/O ports integrated onto a single monolithic IC (e.g. 8051, ATmega328P, STM32).

knowledgeDocuments.summary: Mechanical technical interview questions for GET (Graduate Engineer Trainee) drives.
knowledgeDocuments.content:
Essential Mechanical Engineering Placement Concepts:
1. Zeroth Law: Establishes thermal equilibrium and temperature measurement.
2. First Law: Conservation of energy (dQ = dU + dW for closed systems).
3. Second Law:
   - Kelvin-Planck statement: Impossible to construct an engine operating in a cycle that absorbs heat from a single reservoir and produces an equivalent amount of work.
   - Clausius statement: Impossible to construct a cyclic device that transfers heat from a lower temperature body to a higher temperature body without external work input.
4. Modes of Heat Transfer:
   - Conduction (Fourier's Law: Q = -k * A * dT/dx)
   - Convection (Newton's Law of Cooling: Q = h * A * (Ts - Tinf))
   - Radiation (Stefan-Boltzmann Law: E = epsilon * sigma * A * T^4)

knowledgeDocuments.title: Data Structures & Algorithms: Complete Placement Preparation Roadmap
knowledgeDocuments.summary: A structured placement syllabus covering linear data structures, non-linear hierarchical structures, dynamic programming, and algorithmic paradigms.
knowledgeDocuments.content:
Data Structures & Algorithms Placement Framework:
Phase 1: Foundations & Complexity Analysis
Master Big-O, Big-Omega, and Big-Theta notations. Learn the difference between worst-case, average-case, and amortized time complexity. Understand space complexity, including auxiliary space versus input space, and how the recursion call stack impacts memory usage.

Phase 2: Linear Data Structures
1. Arrays & Dynamic Vectors: Contiguous memory, cache locality, prefix sum arrays, two-pointer techniques, and Kadane's algorithm for maximum subarray sum.
2. Strings: Character manipulation, rolling hash (Rabin-Karp), sliding window for substring problems, and Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP) pattern matching.
3. Linked Lists: Singly, doubly, and circular linked lists. Fast and slow pointer technique (Floyd's cycle detection algorithm) to find cycles and midpoints in O(1) space.
4. Stacks & Queues: LIFO vs FIFO principles. Monotonic stack for Next Greater Element and Largest Rectangle in Histogram. Circular queues and deques for sliding window minimums/maximums.
5. Hashing: Hash tables, collision resolution via separate chaining vs open addressing (linear probing, quadratic probing, double hashing). Amortized O(1) average lookup.

Phase 3: Hierarchical & Non-Linear Structures
1. Trees & BSTs: Binary tree properties, DFS traversals (inorder, preorder, postorder) and BFS level order traversal. Binary Search Trees (BST) invariant: left < root < right. Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) and height-balanced AVL/Red-Black tree concepts.
2. Heaps & Priority Queues: Complete binary tree representation in an array. Min-heap and Max-heap. Building a heap in O(N) linear time using sift-down. Finding the Top-K elements and running median from data streams.
3. Graphs: Adjacency list vs adjacency matrix representations. Breadth-First Search (BFS) for shortest path in unweighted graphs. Depth-First Search (DFS) for connectivity. Cycle detection in directed graphs using topological sorting (Kahn's algorithm) or 3-color DFS. Dijkstra's algorithm for shortest paths with non-negative edge weights using a min-heap in O((V + E) log V).
4. Advanced Structures: Tries (Prefix Trees) for dictionary searches and prefix lookups in O(L) time where L is word length. Disjoint Set Union (DSU / Union-Find) with path compression and union by rank achieving nearly linear O(alpha(V)) time, widely used in Kruskal's Minimum Spanning Tree algorithm.

Phase 4: Core Algorithmic Paradigms
1. Searching & Sorting: Binary search on answer space, rotated sorted arrays, and lower/upper bounds. QuickSort partitioning (Lomuto vs Hoare) and MergeSort divide-and-conquer.
2. Dynamic Programming: Optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems. Top-down memoization vs bottom-up tabulation. Standard classics: 0/1 Knapsack, Longest Common Subsequence (LCS), Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS), and Matrix Chain Multiplication.
3. Greedy Algorithms: Greedy choice property. Interval scheduling, Activity Selection, Fractional Knapsack, and Huffman Coding.
4. Backtracking: Exploring decision trees with pruning. Classic problems: N-Queens, Sudoku Solver, Rat in a Maze, and generating permutations/subsets.

knowledgeDocuments.title: Data Structures: Hashing, Collision Resolution & Open Addressing
knowledgeDocuments.summary: Comprehensive analysis of hash functions, separate chaining, open addressing (linear probing, quadratic probing, double hashing), load factor management, and rehashing.
knowledgeDocuments.content:
Hashing is a fundamental technique to achieve average-case O(1) insertion, deletion, and search operations.
1. Hash Functions:
A good hash function maps large keys uniformly across the table slots, minimizing clustering. Common methods include the Division Method (h(k) = k mod m, where m is prime) and the Multiplication Method.

2. Collision Resolution Techniques:
When two keys hash to the same bucket (h(k1) == h(k2)), collisions must be resolved:
A. Separate Chaining (Open Hashing):
Each bucket in the hash table points to a linked list (or balanced BST in Java 8+ HashMap when bucket size exceeds 8).
- Advantages: Simple to implement, table never fills up completely, less sensitive to load factor alpha.
- Disadvantages: Cache misses due to pointer chasing, extra memory overhead for pointers.

B. Open Addressing (Closed Hashing):
All elements are stored directly inside the hash table array. If a collision occurs, alternative slots are systematically probed:
- Linear Probing: h(k, i) = (h'(k) + i) mod m. Suffers from Primary Clustering (long contiguous runs of occupied slots build up, degrading performance to O(N)).
- Quadratic Probing: h(k, i) = (h'(k) + c1*i + c2*i^2) mod m. Reduces primary clustering but suffers from Secondary Clustering (keys hashing to the same starting slot follow the exact same probe sequence).
- Double Hashing: h(k, i) = (h1(k) + i * h2(k)) mod m. Best open addressing method. Uses a second hash function h2(k) that must never evaluate to 0 and must be relatively prime to table size m. Eliminates both primary and secondary clustering.

3. Load Factor (alpha) & Rehashing:
Load factor alpha = n / m (where n is the number of keys and m is table size). In open addressing, alpha must be strictly less than 1 (typically kept under 0.7). When alpha exceeds the threshold, rehashing is triggered: a new table of approximately 2x size (prime) is allocated, and all keys are recomputed and re-inserted.

knowledgeDocuments.title: Advanced Data Structures: Tries (Prefix Trees) & Disjoint Set Union (DSU)
knowledgeDocuments.summary: Implementation details and asymptotic complexities of Trie (Prefix Tree) and Disjoint Set Union (DSU) with Path Compression and Union by Rank.
knowledgeDocuments.content:
Advanced Data Structures frequently tested in Product Company Interviews:

1. Trie (Prefix Tree):
A Trie is an efficient tree-like data structure used for storing and retrieving strings over an alphabet (e.g., lowercase English letters a-z).
- Structure: Each node contains an array of child pointers (children[26]) or a hash map, and a boolean flag isEndOfWord.
- Operations:
  * Insert(word): Traverse node by node. If character node does not exist, create it. Mark last node isEndOfWord = true. Time: O(L), Space: O(L * alphabet_size) where L is string length.
  * Search(word): Traverse characters. If any child pointer is null, return false. Return isEndOfWord at the end. Time: O(L).
  * StartsWith(prefix): Identical to search, but returns true as long as prefix traversal succeeds, regardless of isEndOfWord. Time: O(L).
- Applications: Autocomplete search suggestions, spell checkers, IP routing longest-prefix match, and Bitwise Trie for maximum XOR pair queries.

2. Disjoint Set Union (DSU / Union-Find):
DSU tracks a partition of elements into disjoint (non-overlapping) subsets.
- Primary Operations:
  * Find(x): Determines which set element x belongs to by returning the representative (root) of its set.
  * Union(x, y): Merges the set containing x with the set containing y.
- Optimizations:
  * Path Compression (in Find): During find(x), redirect all traversed nodes to point directly to the root: parent[x] = find(parent[x]). Flattens tree height dramatically.
  * Union by Rank / Size (in Union): Attach the shorter tree under the root of the taller tree. Prevents tree degeneration into a linked list.
- Time Complexity: With both Path Compression and Union by Rank, any sequence of m operations on n elements runs in O(m * alpha(n)) time, where alpha is the Inverse Ackermann function. In practice, alpha(n) <= 4 for all realistic values of n (even greater than the number of atoms in the universe), making operations effectively O(1) amortized.
- Applications: Kruskal's Minimum Spanning Tree algorithm, detecting cycles in undirected graphs, and dynamic connectivity in networks.

knowledgeDocuments.title: Operating Systems: Process Scheduling, Concurrency & Deadlocks (Coffman Conditions)
knowledgeDocuments.summary: Comprehensive placement guide covering CPU scheduling algorithms (Round Robin, SRTF), synchronization primitives (Mutex, Semaphore), and Coffman deadlock conditions with Banker algorithm.
knowledgeDocuments.content:
Operating Systems Concurrency, Scheduling, and Deadlock Management:
1. CPU Scheduling Algorithms:
- First-Come, First-Served (FCFS): Non-preemptive, suffers from the Convoy Effect.
- Shortest Job First (SJF) / Shortest Remaining Time First (SRTF): Optimal minimum average waiting time. Preemptive SJF is SRTF. Can cause starvation of long processes.
- Round Robin (RR): Preemptive, time-sliced allocation with a quantum q. Fair, interactive, performance heavily depends on quantum size (too large -> FCFS, too small -> context switch overhead).
- Priority Scheduling: Preemptive or non-preemptive. Suffers from starvation; resolved via Aging (gradually increasing the priority of waiting processes).

2. Critical Section Problem & Synchronization:
A critical section must satisfy Mutual Exclusion, Progress, and Bounded Waiting.
- Mutex: Locking mechanism with ownership (only the thread that locked the mutex can unlock it).
- Semaphore: Signaling mechanism. Counting semaphore maintains an integer count; Binary semaphore acts like a mutex (0 or 1) without ownership enforcement.

3. Deadlocks & The Four Coffman Conditions:
A deadlock state occurs if and only if all four Coffman conditions hold simultaneously:
1. Mutual Exclusion: At least one resource must be held in a non-shareable mode.
2. Hold and Wait: A process holding at least one resource is actively waiting to acquire additional resources held by other processes.
3. No Preemption: Resources cannot be forcibly confiscated from a process; they can only be released voluntarily.
4. Circular Wait: A closed chain of processes exists such that each process holds a resource needed by the next process in the cycle (P0 -> P1 -> P2 -> ... -> P0).

Deadlock Handling Strategies:
- Prevention: Invalidate at least one of the four Coffman conditions (e.g., impose a global linear ordering on all resource acquisitions to eliminate Circular Wait).
- Avoidance: Ensure the system never enters an Unsafe State using Dijkstra's Banker's Algorithm (allocating resources only if a safe execution sequence of processes exists).
- Detection & Recovery: Allow deadlocks to occur, detect cycles using a Resource Allocation Graph (Wait-For Graph), and terminate processes or preempt resources.

knowledgeDocuments.title: Computer Networks: OSI 7-Layer Model, TCP/IP Suite & Handshake Protocols
knowledgeDocuments.summary: Core networking interview preparation covering OSI vs TCP/IP layer responsibilities, TCP 3-way handshake, SYN flood mitigation, UDP comparison, and DNS resolution.
knowledgeDocuments.content:
Computer Networks Core Protocol Architecture:
1. OSI 7-Layer vs TCP/IP Protocol Stack:
- Application Layer: HTTP/HTTPS, DNS, FTP, SMTP, SSH (Data units: Messages).
- Transport Layer: End-to-end communication, port addressing, flow & error control. TCP (reliable, connection-oriented, byte-stream) vs UDP (unreliable, connectionless, datagram). (Data units: Segments / Datagrams).
- Network Layer: Logical host-to-host addressing (IPv4/IPv6), packet routing (OSPF, BGP). (Data units: Packets).
- Data Link Layer: Node-to-node framing, physical MAC addressing, error detection via CRC, CSMA/CD. (Data units: Frames).
- Physical Layer: Raw binary bit transmission over physical media (cables, radio waves). (Data units: Bits).

2. TCP 3-Way Handshake Connection Establishment:
Step 1: Client -> Server: SYN (Synchronize Sequence Number = X, SYN flag = 1).
Step 2: Server -> Client: SYN-ACK (Server Seq = Y, ACK = X + 1, SYN flag = 1, ACK flag = 1).
Step 3: Client -> Server: ACK (Client Seq = X + 1, ACK = Y + 1, ACK flag = 1). Connection ESTABLISHED.
- Security Note: SYN Flood attacks exploit half-open connections; mitigated via SYN Cookies.
- TCP Connection Teardown (4-Way Handshake): FIN -> ACK -> FIN -> ACK (with TIME_WAIT state to ensure final ACK delivery).

3. DNS Resolution Hierarchy:
Client -> Local Recursive Resolver -> Root DNS Server ('.') -> TLD DNS Server ('.com') -> Authoritative DNS Server ('example.com') -> IP Address returned.
